text: I'll start with the paged workload.

arguments.root_cause_statement: Service payments/payments-gateway selects pods with label app=payments-gateway, but the only pods backing it, produced by Deployment payments/payments-gateway-api, carry the label app=payments-gateway-api. Nothing matches the selector, so Endpoints payments/payments-gateway has no addresses and its ClusterIP 10.96.215.202 refuses connections. Deployment storefront/checkout-api resolves its ExternalName Service storefront/payments-gateway to that same cluster IP; every health call to http://payments-gateway:8080/health returns "Connection refused", the container never writes /tmp/ready, its exec readiness probe "test -f /tmp/ready" keeps failing, and both checkout-api pods stay Ready=False, so the deployment reports 0/2 and order submissions fail.
arguments.mechanism: Service payments/payments-gateway has .spec.selector.app = "payments-gateway" while the pods of Deployment payments/payments-gateway-api are labelled app=payments-gateway-api, so no pod matches and Endpoints payments/payments-gateway is created with no subsets; its ClusterIP 10.96.215.202 therefore has no backend and TCP connects to port 8080 are answered "Connection refused" instead of reaching the gateway. The selector should read app=payments-gateway-api to match the pod template labels.

ruled_out.alternative: The gateway pods themselves are down or unhealthy
ruled_out.ruling_claim: Both gateway pods are Running and Ready, so the backend workload is healthy.

ruled_out.alternative: The storefront ExternalName service points at the wrong DNS name
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The ExternalName correctly names payments-gateway.payments.svc.cluster.local, and DNS resolved it to the payments service ClusterIP 10.96.215.202 seen in the logs.

ruled_out.alternative: A NetworkPolicy in payments blocks traffic from storefront
ruled_out.ruling_claim: No NetworkPolicy objects exist in the payments namespace.
ruled_out.quote: 0 objects of kind networkpolicies in namespace payments

ruled_out.alternative: The checkout-api pod spec is broken (missing ConfigMap or bad mount)
ruled_out.ruling_claim: ConfigMap storefront/checkout-scripts exists with the run.sh key the pod mounts, and the container started normally.

verification.command: kubectl -n payments get svc payments-gateway -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'

evidence.claim: The name payments-gateway that checkout-api calls is a Service in storefront that is an ExternalName alias for the payments namespace service, which is how storefront depends on payments.
The refused IP 10.96.215.202 is the ClusterIP of the aliased Service payments/payments-gateway.
Service payments/payments-gateway selects a label no pod carries and has zero endpoint addresses.
The gateway pods are labelled app=payments-gateway-api, not app=payments-gateway.
The Deployment pod template labels those pods app=payments-gateway-api.
